title: ScamBuster TTP Taxonomy Artifact
description: The machine-readable form of the ScamBuster scammer-side TTP taxonomy. Generated from the canonical seed by scambuster:ttp:taxonomy-export; never hand-edited. One file per taxonomy version.

taxonomy_version.description: Semantic version of the taxonomy. MAJOR = meaning change or deprecation of a code; MINOR = new codes or phases; PATCH = wording fixes that change no meaning. See docs/standards/taxonomy-versioning.md.

generated_from.description: The canonical source constant this artifact was generated from. Present so a consumer can see the file is derived, not authored.

kill_chain_name.description: The kill chain name carried by every exported STIX attack-pattern. Renaming it is a breaking change for consumers and is a MAJOR taxonomy change.

phases.description: The kill-chain phases, in scam-progression order. The order is semantic: it is the sequence a scam conversation moves through.

entry_count.description: Number of entries in this artifact. Redundant with entries.length on purpose: a consumer reading a truncated file notices.

code.description: Stable first-party identifier. Codes are never reused and never deleted; a retired code stays with active=false.

label.description: Short human-readable name. Unique across the taxonomy.

definition.description: What the behaviour is, as an annotator applies it. This is the text a scoring verdict is judged against.

phase.description: Kill-chain phase. Must be one of the values in the top-level phases list.

examples.description: Illustrative phrasings. Illustrations only: an annotator matches the definition, not this list.

stimulus_affinity.description: Which conversational stimuli this behaviour tends to follow. Temporal, never causal: an affinity says the behaviour is observed after the stimulus, not that the stimulus caused it.

external_refs.description: Mappings to external knowledge bases. Only sources with a per-entry, dated, recorded mapping check appear here (see docs/standards/f3-mapping.md). An absent reference means no verified mapping exists, never that one was omitted.

active.description: False marks a deprecated entry. Deprecated entries keep their code and their STIX id so historical observations stay interpretable.

stix_id.description: Deterministic STIX 2.1 attack-pattern id (UUIDv5 over the code, seeded with the taxonomy major version). Stable within a taxonomy major version; a new major mints fresh ids.

source_name.description: The knowledge base. Closed set: adding a source means adding a recorded per-entry mapping exercise for it.

external_id.description: The technique identifier in that knowledge base. The same id may legitimately appear under two source names: F3 references ATT&CK techniques where they apply to fraud, and the two are different knowledge bases.
